sections.title: Background

summary.text: Gives the background to the cervical cancer guideline, citing about 604,000 new cases and 342,000 deaths in 2020, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa, Melanesia, South-Eastern Asia and South America. It recalls the Director-General's 2018 call for elimination and the 2020 global strategy targets, and notes that experts agreed to update and simplify screening and treatment recommendations.

sections.extract: Cervical cancer is a leading cause of mortality among women. In 2020, an estimated 604 000 women were diagnosed with cervical cancer worldwide and about 342 000 women died from the disease. Cervical cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer in 23 countries and is the leading cause of cancer death in 36 countries. It describes the work of the Guideline Development Group from 2019 and defines the screen-and-treat and screen, triage and treat approaches.

sections.title: Summary of screening and treatment recommendations to prevent cervical cancer

summary.text: Summarises the guideline's 23 recommendations and 7 good practice statements, explaining which apply identically to the general population of women and which differ for women living with HIV. A table pairs the recommendations for each group, starting with the strong recommendation to use HPV DNA detection rather than VIA or cytology as the primary screening test, followed by guidance on triage options, self-collected samples, starting age, screening intervals and follow-up. It gives the strength of each recommendation and certainty of evidence. It ends with summary strategies: HPV DNA screening from age 30 every 5 to 10 years for women generally, and from age 25 every 3 to 5 years with triage for women living with HIV.

sections.title: Background

summary.text: Restates the global burden of cervical cancer and the 2030 elimination targets of 90% HPV vaccination, 70% screening and 90% treatment. It explains that cervical intraepithelial neoplasia is caused mainly by high-risk HPV types such as 16 and 18 and distinguishes low-grade lesions from high-grade pre-cancers.

sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Reviews cervical screening methods, noting that cytology programmes have greatly cut mortality in some countries but have been less successful in low- and middle-income settings, and describes newer VIA and HPV DNA tests and tests under evaluation. A table groups molecular, cytologic and visual inspection tests, and the text explains the screen-and-treat approach, preferably in a single visit.

sections.title: Approaches to screening and treatment

summary.text: Defines the two approaches compared in the guideline: screen-and-treat, where treatment follows a positive primary test, and screen, triage and treat, which requires a second positive triage test.

sections.extract: In this document, two approaches to screening and treatment are distinguished: the screen-and-treat approach and the screen, triage and treat approach. Screening and treatment approaches • In the “screen-and-treat approach”, the decision to treat is based on a positive primary screening test only. • In the “screen, triage and treat approach”, the decision to treat is based on a positive primary screening test

sections.title: Rationale for this new edition of recommendations

summary.text: Explains that earlier WHO cervical screening and treatment recommendations were spread across several guidelines and the 2014 comprehensive guide, and that this edition updates them in light of new evidence and the elimination strategy. It states the guideline's objective of improving national screening and treatment strategies for all women, including those living with HIV.

sections.extract: Recommendations for screening and treatment to prevent cervical cancer, including for women living with HIV, can be found in four existing WHO guidelines – on screening and treatment of pre-cancer lesions, treatment for CIN2/3 and AIS, cryotherapy for CIN, and thermal ablation for pre-cancer lesions (12–15). summary.text: Outlines the four phases of updating WHO's cervical screening recommendations, from updating key algorithms (this guideline) to evaluating others, implementation guidance and a living guideline. It notes that the guideline also aims to clarify starting age, lifetime screens and screening intervals.

sections.extract: The following are the four phases of the updates to WHO’s cervical cancer screening and treatment recommendations. This guideline delivers the output of Phase 1. sections.title: Target audience

summary.text: Identifies the guideline's audience as policy-makers, programme managers and health professionals involved in cervical cancer prevention, and notes that the term women is used for all people at risk of cervical cancer regardless of gender identity.

sections.extract: This document is intended primarily for policy-makers, programme managers, programme officers and other professionals in the health sector who have responsibility for choosing strategies for cervical cancer prevention, at country, regional and district levels. summary.text: Advises that a multidisciplinary ministry team choose national screening algorithms according to resources, feasibility and acceptability, and distinguishes clinical scenarios for follow-up such as regular screening intervals. It encourages population-based programmes that ensure treatment of women who screen positive.

The choice will vary by country – and in different settings within country programmes – and will depend on available resources, feasibility and acceptability. sections.title: Screening and triage tests considered in these guidelines

summary.text: Describes the screening and triage tests considered, including high-risk HPV DNA tests with partial or extended genotyping, cytology, VIA and colposcopy. It explains how they are combined in algorithms, such as HPV testing followed by VIA triage to decide treatment.

sections.extract: High-risk HPV DNA tests: These tests identify a group of high-risk carcinogenic HPV genotypes, typically including up to 14 types (HPV16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58 and 59, which are Group 1 carcinogens, and HPV66 and 68) (37). sections.title: Treatment considerations

summary.text: Explains treatment options for cervical pre-cancer, distinguishing ablative methods (thermal ablation, cryotherapy) from excisional ones (LLETZ, cold knife conization), and restates the count of recommendations and good practice statements.

sections.extract: In a screen-and-treat approach, women who screen positive are treated without histological diagnosis. The treatment aims to destroy or remove the transformation zone of the cervix, or remove areas of the cervix that have been identified as abnormal by screening. The methods of treatment may be ablative (destroying abnormal tissue by heating it with thermal coagulation or freezing it with cryotherapy) or excisional

sections.title: Justification

summary.text: Explains the justification for the recommendations, chiefly the greater reductions in cancer and deaths with HPV DNA testing than with VIA or cytology, possible fewer harms and the acceptability of provider or self-sampling. It also justifies the chosen starting age, intervals and follow-up timings, based mostly on low-certainty evidence and modelling.

sections.extract: A strong recommendation was made for using HPV DNA detection as a primary screening test when part of a screen-and-treat approach or a screen, triage and treat approach because a higher value was placed on the greater reductions in cervical cancer and deaths that are likely with HPV DNA detection compared with using VIA or cytology as a primary screening test (moderate- certainty evidence). There may also be fewer

sections.title: Summary of the evidence

summary.text: Summarises the evidence behind the cervical screening recommendations for the general population of women, finding moderate-certainty evidence from trials and modelling that HPV DNA testing reduces pre-cancer, advanced cancer and deaths more than VIA, with lower risk after a negative HPV test than after negative cytology. It reports similar benefits for screen-and-treat and triage approaches, slightly fewer cancers with HPV16/18 genotyping triage, and likely similar performance of self-collected samples. It reviews evidence on starting screening at 30 versus 35, stopping age, screening intervals and follow-up timing, weighing benefits against treatments, preterm births and costs. It notes practical concerns about longer follow-up intervals and the transition from VIA or cytology to HPV testing.

summary.text: Justifies the recommendations for women living with HIV, citing the greater cancer and death reductions from HPV DNA testing, its acceptability and feasibility, and the reduced harms from adding triage. It also explains the chosen screening intervals and follow-up timings, mostly on low-certainty modelled evidence.

sections.title: Summary of the evidence

summary.text: Summarises the evidence for the recommendations for women living with HIV, finding that HPV DNA primary screening likely reduces pre-cancer more than VIA and similarly to cytology, and that triage may reduce harms through fewer treatments. It reports modelled benefits of three- to five-year intervals, the likely validity of self-sampling, and a good practice statement to screen at least twice in a lifetime. It also reviews individual patient data and modelling on starting age, follow-up intervals and uncertainties in applying general population results.

sections.title: Justification and evidence summary

summary.text: Summarises low-certainty evidence showing little difference in recurrence or complications between cold knife conization and loop excision for adenocarcinoma in situ, but more preterm births after conization, which is also costlier and less accessible. It then lists research gaps on HPV genotyping, screening strategies and starting age for women living with HIV.

sections.title: Annex 5. Standardized definitions used in this guideline

summary.text: Annex 5, giving the standardised definitions used in the guideline, starting with eligibility for ablative treatment based on transformation zone type and lesion size and criteria for referral. It defines outcomes such as persistent, residual or recurrent disease and other clinical endpoints used in the reviews. It also defines the treatment methods, including thermal ablation, cryotherapy, LLETZ, cold knife conization and small-loop biopsy. Diagrams illustrate the three types of transformation zone.

sections.extract: DEFINITIONS USED IN THIS GUIDELINE 5.1. Eligibility for ablative treatment Women who screen positive with a human papillomavirus (HPV) nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) are assessed for eligibility for ablative treatment so that women with or without a visible lesion (or lesions), who are eligible for ablation, can receive an ablative treatment (see section 5.1.2). sections.title: Annex 6. Additional information for screening and treatment recommendations

summary.text: Annex 6, giving additional information on quality assurance, screening registries and call-and-recall, and describing the screening tests in more detail, including self-collection of samples, HPV nucleic acid tests and genotyping, cytology and VIA. It advises care in selecting clinically validated HPV tests and ends with footnoted references and WHO contact details.

narratives.fr: Trois schémas du col de l’utérus vu de face, disposés verticalement : un cercle rose comportant une zone rouge centrale de taille et de position variables autour de l’orifice, chacun avec des lignes de repère dont les étiquettes ne figurent pas dans l’image. Dans le texte de l’annexe, ces schémas accompagnent la description des types 1, 2 et 3 de zone de remaniement.
narratives.ru: Три схематических изображения шейки матки во фронтальной проекции, расположенные вертикально: розовый круг с центральной красной областью разного размера и положения вокруг зева, у каждого — выносные линии, подписи к которым в изображение не входят. В окружающем тексте приложения такие рисунки сопровождают описание зон трансформации 1, 2 и 3 типов.

narratives.en: Three schematic cross-section drawings of the cervix and cervical canal, stacked vertically, with red segments marking the epithelium at and inside the canal opening to differing extents and leader lines whose labels are not part of the image. They appear alongside the front-view drawings of transformation zone types 1, 2 and 3.
narratives.ar: ثلاثة رسوم تخطيطية لمقاطع عرضية لعنق الرحم وقناته، مرتبة عمودياً، مع أجزاء حمراء تشير إلى الظهارة عند فتحة القناة وداخلها بدرجات متفاوتة، وخطوط إشارة لا تظهر تسمياتها في الصورة. وتظهر إلى جانب الرسوم الأمامية لأنواع منطقة التحول 1 و2 و3.
narratives.zh: 三幅纵向排列的子宫颈及宫颈管剖面示意图，红色线段标示宫颈管开口处及管内不同范围的上皮，并带有引线，但其标签不在图像中。这些图与1型、2型和3型转化区的正面示意图并列。
narratives.es: Tres dibujos esquemáticos en corte del cuello uterino y el conducto cervical, dispuestos verticalmente, con segmentos rojos que marcan el epitelio en la abertura del conducto y en su interior en distinta medida, y líneas de referencia cuyas etiquetas no forman parte de la imagen. Aparecen junto a los dibujos frontales de los tipos 1, 2 y 3 de zona de transformación.
narratives.fr: Trois schémas en coupe du col de l’utérus et du canal cervical, disposés verticalement, avec des segments rouges marquant l’épithélium à l’ouverture du canal et à l’intérieur, à des degrés divers, et des lignes de repère dont les étiquettes ne figurent pas dans l’image. Ils accompagnent les schémas de face des types 1, 2 et 3 de zone de remaniement.
narratives.ru: Три схематических изображения шейки матки и цервикального канала в разрезе, расположенные вертикально; красными сегментами в разной степени отмечен эпителий у входа в канал и внутри него, имеются выносные линии, подписи к которым в изображение не входят. Они расположены рядом с фронтальными изображениями зон трансформации 1, 2 и 3 типов.

columns.titles: For both the general population and women living with HIV
Strength of recommendation and certainty of evidence

rows:
41. Once a decision to treat a woman is made – whether from the general population of women or women living with HIV – it is good practice to treat as soon as possible within six months to reduce the risk of loss to follow-up. However, in women who are pregnant, good practice includes deferral until after pregnancy.
In circumstances when treatment is not provided within this time frame, it is good practice to re-evaluate the woman before treatment.

42. WHO suggests large-loop excision of the transformation zone (LLETZ) or cold knife conization (CKC) for women from the general population and women living with HIV who have histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS).
Remarks: Loop excision may be preferred in women of reproductive age, in settings with greater availability of LLETZ and by providers with greater expertise performing LLETZ. CKC may be preferred when interpretation of the margins of the histological specimen is imperative.

narratives.en: The table gives one good practice statement (no. 41, on the timing of treatment) and one recommendation (no. 42, on excision treatment for adenocarcinoma in situ) that apply to both the general population of women and women living with HIV, with the strength of recommendation and certainty of evidence.
narratives.ar: يعرض الجدول بيان ممارسة جيدة واحداً (رقم 41، بشأن توقيت العلاج) وتوصية واحدة (رقم 42، بشأن العلاج بالاستئصال للسرطانة الغدية الموضعية) ينطبقان على عموم النساء وعلى النساء المصابات بفيروس العوز المناعي البشري، مع بيان قوة التوصية ودرجة اليقين في البيّنات.
narratives.zh: 该表列出一项良好实践声明（第41条，关于治疗时机）和一项建议（第42条，关于原位腺癌的切除治疗），二者均适用于一般女性人群和感染艾滋病毒的女性，并注明建议强度和证据确定性。
narratives.es: La tabla presenta una declaración de buenas prácticas (n.º 41, sobre el momento del tratamiento) y una recomendación (n.º 42, sobre el tratamiento por escisión del adenocarcinoma in situ) aplicables tanto a la población general de mujeres como a las mujeres con VIH, con la fuerza de la recomendación y la certeza de la evidencia.
narratives.fr: Le tableau présente une déclaration de bonne pratique (no 41, sur le délai de traitement) et une recommandation (no 42, sur le traitement par excision de l’adénocarcinome in situ) s’appliquant à la fois à la population générale des femmes et aux femmes vivant avec le VIH, avec la force de la recommandation et le degré de certitude des données.
narratives.ru: В таблице приведены одно положение о надлежащей практике (№ 41, о сроках лечения) и одна рекомендация (№ 42, о лечении аденокарциномы in situ путем иссечения), применимые как к женщинам из общей популяции, так и к женщинам, живущим с ВИЧ, с указанием силы рекомендации и степени достоверности данных.

narratives.fr: Le tableau énumère les sept algorithmes prioritaires de dépistage et de traitement évalués pour la ligne directrice, regroupés en approches « dépister et traiter » (1–2) et « dépister, trier et traiter » (3–7).
narratives.ru: В таблице перечислены семь приоритетных алгоритмов скрининга и лечения, оцененных для руководства, сгруппированных в подходы «скрининг и лечение» (1–2) и «скрининг, сортировка и лечение» (3–7).
